title: Once upon a time
goal: Recognize -mIş on verbs in news, discoveries and folk tales: gelmiş, kar yağmış, bir varmış bir yokmuş.

intro.text: Verbs take `-mIş` too: *Ali gelmiş* (Ali has come, it seems: you see his coat), *Kar yağmış!* (It's snowed: you wake up to white streets). Folk tales use it all the way through: *Bir varmış, bir yokmuş…* (Once there was, once there wasn't…).

exercises.question: You come home and see your older brother's shoes at the door. What do you say?

why.1: *Geldi* fits if you saw him arrive.
why.2: *Geliyor* means he is on his way.

exercises.explain: You work it out from his shoes, so `-mIş`: *gelmiş*.

exercises.en: Once there was, once there wasn't.

reject.why: Folk tales tell what nobody saw, so `-mIş`: *varmış*.
The last vowel of *yok* is o, rounded and back: *yokmuş*.

exercises.explain: The opening of Turkish folk tales: *varmış* and *yokmuş*, each in harmony with its word.
`-mIş` starts with a consonant, so *git-* keeps its t: *gitmiş*.

exercises.en: One day Keloğlan went to the city.

exercises.question: Who did Keloğlan marry?

context.tr: Bir varmış, bir yokmuş. Bir köyde fakir bir kadın ve oğlu varmış.
context.en: Once there was, once there wasn't. In a village there lived a poor woman and her son.

context.tr: Oğlanın adı Keloğlan'mış. Keloğlan çok akıllıymış.
context.en: The boy's name was Keloğlan. Keloğlan was very clever.

context.tr: Bir gün padişahın kızı köye gelmiş. Keloğlan kızı görmüş.
context.en: One day the sultan's daughter came to the village. Keloğlan saw the girl.
In the end Keloğlan married the sultan's daughter.

options: a poor woman from the village
exercises.explain: *Padişahın kızıyla evlenmiş*: he married the sultan's daughter. *Evlenmek* takes `-(y)lA`: *kızıyla*.

exercises.prompt: Apparently Elif has gone to Istanbul.

reject.why: *Gitti* says you know it first-hand. **Apparently** calls for `-mIş`: *gitmiş*.

exercises.en: The sultan had three daughters, the tale says.

reject.why: The last vowel of *var* is a: *-mış*.

accept: Once there was a poor man.
There once was a poor man.
Once upon a time there was a poor man.

exercises.label: *gelmek* + `-mIş`: it seems I came, it seems you came…

exercises.prompt: One day Keloğlan became rich. (in a folk tale)

reject.why: In a folk tale, keep to `-mIş`: *olmuş*.

exercises.question: *Uyumuşum.* When do you say it?
options: When you realize you fell asleep without noticing
When you slept well every night
When you want to go to sleep
exercises.explain: With *ben*, `-mIş` means you realize it only afterwards: **I must have fallen asleep**.
